adversarial_replay.command: node run-adversarial.mjs against isolated candidate-937 sandbox
adversarial_replay.interpretation: These are contract probes against the candidate implementation, not claims about production data or independent scientific acceptance.

findings.title: A success claim accepts a command with a nonzero or failed result
findings.evidence: The schema requires only a non-empty command result; exit_code, completion_status, timestamps and expected/actual are optional. Both validators only test that command.result is non-empty. In the adversarial success_with_nonzero_exit case, exit_code=1 and completion_status=failed still returned ok=true/outcome=accepted.
findings.impact: A producer_checked or passed acceptance result can be backed by an actually failed command.
findings.recommendation: For success states require exit_code=0 when numeric, or an explicit recognized success completion status when no numeric exit exists; reject conflicts and add a negative fixture. Require actual command timing and expected/actual evidence for completed checks.

findings.title: Repository source identity hashing has incomplete locality and symlink enforcement
findings.evidence: The checker skips any source identity without sha256 (L452-L453), classifies only IDs containing '/' or starting '.' as repository paths (L454-L460), and hashes a contained lexical path without realpath containment (L464-L475). A root-level root-source.txt with a wrong SHA, an omitted SHA, and a repository symlink to an outside file all returned ok=true in the adversarial replay.
findings.impact: Invalid or absent source evidence can be accepted, and an outside file can satisfy a repository-path identity through a symlink.
findings.recommendation: Make local versus external source identity explicit, require SHA and resolved containment for every local path, and reject outside symlink targets. Add root-level, omitted-hash and symlink negative fixtures.

findings.title: Changed-file containment is lexical only
findings.evidence: evaluateChangedFiles calls resolveContainedPath and then existsAsFile, but never realpath-checks the result. A changed_files entry pointing to a symlink outside the repository returned ok=true and changed_file_containment=passed.
findings.impact: The implementation contradicts its own header claim of lexical and symlink-resolved containment and allows an outside path to be presented as a changed repository file.
findings.recommendation: Resolve each changed path and enforce realRoot containment before accepting it; retain a separate typed deletion outcome for genuinely absent paths.

findings.title: A completed handoff with no evidence arrays is accepted
findings.evidence: commands, artifacts, acceptance_results, changed_files, commits and source_identities have no minItems requirements, and status is only a non-empty string. The empty_evidence_arrays case set all evidence arrays empty while retaining status producer_checked; checker returned ok=true with no findings. unknown_status_and_null_owner also returned ok=true because status is unconstrained and owner is nullable.
findings.impact: A packet can advertise a completed producer state without a command, acceptance result, artifact or attributable owner.
findings.recommendation: Constrain handoff status to the protocol state enum, require a non-null owner for producer states, and impose status-specific minimum evidence (at least acceptance/command/artifact records for success claims). Preserve explicit blocked/unresolved packets with required reasons.

findings.title: Duplicate IDs and command event_source are not bound
findings.evidence: The schemas do not require unique command or artifact IDs. The checker converts both arrays to Maps, silently keeping the last duplicate. A duplicate conflicting command ID and a command event_source object pointing to a nonexistent artifact both returned ok=true; event_source is never cross-referenced or hashed.
findings.impact: A command or artifact reference can become ambiguous, and an embedded command evidence pointer can be fabricated without resolution.
findings.recommendation: Reject duplicate IDs before Map construction and either resolve event_source against artifacts or remove the unused field. Add conflicting-duplicate and unbound-event-source fixtures.

findings.title: Ledger fallback leaves the handoff base SHA unbound
findings.evidence: When no sibling task-binding exists, resolveAuthorities falls back to ledger dependency SHAs with effective.base_sha=null. evaluateDependencyBinding then marks base_sha_binding not_applicable and only checks that the claimed base is a local commit with dependency ancestry. Moving the valid packet outside its sibling task-binding directory and changing base_sha from e5c44249 to local commit 601072e9 returned ok=true.
findings.impact: A new handoff can claim an arbitrary local base while still passing dependency checks, undermining exact base/dependency binding.
findings.recommendation: Require a sibling task binding for post-schema handoffs, or add and compare an exact base SHA in the authoritative ledger. Retain an explicit historical compatibility path for PR001/PR002 rather than silently weakening new packets.

findings.title: Command timing, exits and expected/actual observations are optional
findings.evidence: The handoff schema permits started_at and completed_at to be null or omitted, and exit_code, completion_status, expected and actual to be omitted. The valid C1 handoff fixture uses null timestamps even though the protocol requires retained command timing and exit evidence; separate producer receipts carry timing.
findings.impact: The handoff itself can omit the evidence needed to audit when and how its acceptance claim was produced.
findings.recommendation: Require timestamps and expected/actual fields for executed commands, and require either numeric exit_code or an explicit typed completion status. Permit null only for documented provider cases with a durable external event source.
